result.title: ServerBench: How can your coding agents design specialized LLM serving systems?
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) coding agents develop software through experimentation, offering an opportunity to design the serving systems supporting their own operation. Effective serving requires coordinating implementation and operating decisions under session dependencies, latency constraints, and correctness requirements. We introduce ServerBench, a benchmark for agentic design of complete, specialized LLM serving systems. Agents experiment against a common objective, dollars per dollar: latency-qualified token value per dollar of GPU cost. Stateful replay preserves session dependencies, and independent verification checks the submitted system. Across 11 coding-agent models and three deployments, Claude Sonnet 5.5 achieves 2.97 dollars per dollar on Gemma E4B, $4.87\times$ the vLLM reference; 22 of 33 runs yield verified systems, and 13 exceed the strongest baseline. Our analysis identifies three findings: high-value designs coordinate capacity improvements with load selection; agents interpret performance feedback through workload-relevant experiments; and reliable delivery requires verification of the execution paths introduced by optimization. Overall, ServerBench supports systematic study of how agents translate service objectives and feedback into effective, verified serving systems for given task specifications.

AI.brief_summary: ServerBench 提出一个基准，让 coding agent 在会话依赖、延迟与正确性约束下，自行实验并设计完整的 LLM 推理服务系统，以「每美元 GPU 成本所换取的延迟达标 token 价值」为统一目标，并用独立验证检查提交的系统。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作关注服务系统层面的工程实现、吞吐与成本优化，未涉及视觉细节在内部状态中的保留、latent 推理状态的生成与使用或证据筛选与停止决策，其成本目标与验证环节与 LVR 的距离过远，难以形成具体借鉴线索。
